script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. Thursday — here is your SOXX recap. The portfolio closed zero point one one percent down on the session. Ten names in the book, a mixed tape of moves, and one acquisition that is reshaping how this sector thinks about the AI race.

Advanced Micro Devices just bought a Toronto-based AI chip startup. The deal is undisclosed in price, but the strategic signal is loud and direct: inference is the next battleground, and Advanced Micro Devices is not waiting.

No broad macro data was available for Thursday's session. Markets traded on earnings momentum and sector rotation within technology. The Nasdaq finished the session with mixed internals as semiconductor names split across the tape, reflecting ongoing tension between AI capital spending enthusiasm and near-term valuation discipline.

The top story belongs to Advanced Micro Devices, which announced the acquisition of Taalas, a Toronto-based startup focused on specialized silicon for AI inference workloads. Inference — the process of running trained AI models to generate real-time responses — has become the critical next frontier as AI deployment scales beyond the training phase. Taalas develops chips designed to cut computing and memory bottlenecks in exactly that workload. Bank of America noted Thursday that while Nvidia dominates AI chip revenue, Advanced Micro Devices is methodically closing the gap, drawing a direct parallel to how the company spent nearly a decade building into Intel's server dominance before capturing meaningful share. The Taalas deal deepens the full-stack AI platform strategy and adds inference-specific intellectual property that complements the existing GPU lineup. Advanced Micro Devices carries the largest weight in this portfolio at eight point three nine percent — this acquisition matters.

Advanced Micro Devices was up one point five zero percent on the session. The Taalas acquisition drove the headline, adding specialized AI inference capability to a roadmap that Bank of America now describes as increasingly competitive with the market leader. The parallel to the Intel server disruption playbook is not casual — it is a structural argument for long-term share gain. Watch for analyst price target revisions in the next session.

Micron Technology was down one point three one percent on Thursday. A Seeking Alpha piece flagged a valuation rotation argument, suggesting that SK Hynix trades near half of Micron's forward multiple despite leading in high-bandwidth memory. Separately, other coverage noted Micron pared most of its losses even as fellow memory names struggled following mixed guidance from competitors. The high-bandwidth memory narrative remains intact, but the valuation premium is under scrutiny.

Nvidia was down zero point one zero percent on the session, essentially flat. Seeking Alpha maintained a hold rating with a price target of two hundred forty-four dollars, citing AI and data center strength alongside a large investment pipeline, while noting that upside is starting to fade at current levels. Jamie Dimon's commentary on AI capital expenditure fatigue added a cautious macro overlay. The design tools expansion announced late July remains an ongoing catalyst to monitor.

Broadcom was up zero point five five percent on Thursday. No specific news crossed for Broadcom directly, but the session's positive move aligns with broader AI infrastructure sentiment. Upcoming earnings guidance from hyperscalers remains the key watch item for this name.

Intel was down one point two four percent on Thursday. The name continues to trade under pressure as the competitive narrative around AI chip share favors rivals. No direct news crossed, but the Advanced Micro Devices acquisition of Taalas incrementally tightens the competitive landscape Intel faces in inference-adjacent markets.

Applied Materials was down one point two seven percent on the session. No specific news crossed. Equipment names faced modest selling pressure Thursday, consistent with caution around near-term semiconductor capital expenditure pacing. Earnings guidance from equipment customers remains the primary catalyst.

KLA Corporation was up zero point two two percent on Thursday. A quiet session for KLA with no direct news, but the marginal positive move in equipment was a relative outperformer versus peers Applied Materials and Lam Research on the session.

Marvell Technology was down zero point two three percent on Thursday. No news crossed directly. Marvell's custom silicon exposure to hyperscaler AI programs keeps this name tied closely to data center spending cycles. Any hyperscaler earnings commentary in coming sessions is directly relevant.

Lam Research was down zero point five four percent on the session. No direct news crossed. Like Applied Materials, Lam trades on equipment spending cycles, and the broader caution around capital expenditure pacing weighed modestly on the name.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing was up one point zero one percent on Thursday, the second-best performer in the book on the session behind Advanced Micro Devices. No direct news crossed, but the move likely reflects confidence in AI chip fabrication demand volume. Any geopolitical or trade headline crossing the tape remains the primary risk to monitor for this name.

Three data points to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, any analyst reactions to the Advanced Micro Devices Taalas acquisition — price target adjustments will set tone for the name heading into next week. Second, Nvidia's earnings report is approaching on the calendar — any pre-earnings commentary or guidance leaks from data center customers will matter immediately. Third, monitor any Federal Reserve speaker scheduled for Friday, as rate path commentary continues to affect growth and technology sector multiples directly.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch the Advanced Micro Devices acquisition narrative closely — analyst community reaction to the Taalas deal will define sentiment for the largest position in this book heading into the weekend.
